text: A tide describes a recurring rise and fall in water level. A current describes water moving from place to place, and tides can drive currents.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: NOAA National Ocean Service, Tides and Currents; https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/tidescurrents.html. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Wind transfers motion to the ocean's surface, creating currents near coasts and across ocean basins.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: NOAA National Ocean Service, Tides and Currents; https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/tidescurrents.html. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Temperature and salinity change seawater's density. Density contrasts help drive circulation that reaches from the surface to deep water.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: NOAA National Ocean Service, Tides and Currents; https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/tidescurrents.html. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Near new and full Moon, the Sun and Moon's tidal effects reinforce one another, usually giving a larger tidal range. The name spring tide refers to the range, not the season.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: NOAA National Ocean Service, Spring and Neap Tides; https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/springtide.html. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Near the first and third quarter Moon, solar and lunar tidal effects partially oppose one another, usually reducing the difference between high and low water.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: NOAA National Ocean Service, Spring and Neap Tides; https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/springtide.html. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Wind can push surface water away from a coast; water from below rises to replace it.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: NOAA National Ocean Service, Upwelling; https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/upwelling.html. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Upwelled water is often colder and richer in nutrients than surface water, supporting productive coastal food webs.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: NOAA National Ocean Service, Upwelling; https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/upwelling.html. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: An estuary combines river water with seawater. Tides continually change its depth and chemistry, creating a patchwork of habitats.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: NOAA Fisheries, Estuary Habitat; https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/national/habitat-conservation/estuary-habitat. Consulted 2026-10-13.
